title: metadata: unregisterPackage of the host package deletes the environment's own object, view, app, hook and dashboard rows the boot pass stamped with the host (follow-up of #32198)
body:
domain:server#7 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgVSjQBHNkZd6Eqx2XX

Follow-up of #32198. Source: #32812's step-0 design and the epic seat's ruling on it (scope B-all held a precondition that measurement refuted, so #32812 stays on the ten package-slotted types and this card takes the rest). Unreleased: #32198 has not shipped.

## What happens

On a host that declares its package and wires a `DatabaseLoader`, the boot priming pass stamps package-less stored rows of the non-package-slotted types (`object`, `view`, `app`, `hook`, `dashboard`) with the host's package. Since #32198, `unregisterPackage(host)` removes by package, so it deletes those rows: the environment's own items are lost when the host package is unregistered. This is on `main` and survives #32812 (which stops the stamp only for the ten package-slotted types).

## Why #32812 does not take it

Not stamping these types moves who owns them: `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` (around L1942, and the reload path around L1865) reads `metadataService.getDiagnosed('object', name)` and registers the object as a contribution of `_packageId ?? 'metadata-service'`, so an environment `object` row on such a host registers today as the host package's contribution. #32198's card and PR describe only the package-slotted removal, not a use of the stamp on these types.

## Owed

1. Measure every reader of `_packageId` / `_provenance` on these five types on `main` (the object contribution kind above first) and what each answers for a stamped environment row.
2. Stop `unregisterPackage(host)` from deleting environment rows of these types (either stop the stamp with the object-contribution move declared, or keep the stamp and exclude stamped environment rows from the removal); pins red on `main`, green after; FROM → TO for every moved answer.
3. Land before the release that would ship #32198.
